gap: No result ChatGPT got gives today's price at the maker's store for the 18650 chargers it recommends. At XTAR's own US store on 2026-11-08 the VC4SL is $32.90, not the $24.99 ChatGPT showed, the VC2SL is $19.90 and the SC2 is $10.90. Nitecore's store has the UMS4 at $38.95 and the UMS2 at $28.95. The 2-bay Tenergy TN270 ($18.99) charges at only 500 mA per slot, so it costs about the same as the VC2SL but charges a single cell four times slower (500 mA vs 2 A).
standout_why: I compared against besttacticalflashlighttoday.net (updated 2026-10-27), beamandbattery.com, xtar.cc's VX4/VC4SL/VP4L Plus comparison and the 1lumen VC4SL review that ChatGPT cited. besttacticalflashlighttoday and beamandbattery give no prices at all, only 'Check Price on Amazon' links. xtar.cc gives Amazon reference prices dated 2025-07-03 for three models only ($42.99 / $32.99 / $67.99). None of them gives a dated price for the whole set from the makers' stores, and none mentions the Tenergy TN270 or its 500 mA rate. besttacticalflashlighttoday already gives the per-slot currents (VC4SL 1 A with four cells, VC2SL 2 A with one), so the new part is the dated maker prices and the TN270 comparison.
decides: The VC4SL stays the value pick for 4-bay 18650 charging. At $32.90 for four bays it costs less per bay than the Nitecore UMS4 ($38.95) or the XTAR VX4 V2 ($41.99), though the shopper should expect the maker's price rather than ChatGPT's $24.99. For one or two cells, the XTAR SC2 ($10.90) or VC2SL ($19.90) beats our Tenergy TN270 ($18.99) because the TN270 is limited to 500 mA per slot. The VC8S ($59.00) is the pick only for charging eight cells at once. The VP4L Plus ($67.99) is the most expensive and needs a separate 12 V 3 A DC supply.

findings.note: This 2020 review doesn't name the hardware version, so it is earlier than V3. It is the only 4-bay charger here that keeps close to 3 A per bay with four cells loaded, where the VC4SL, UMS4 and VX4 drop to 1 A. Where it loses: needs a barrel-plug wall adapter (no USB-C), and its price could not be sourced from a page I could open.
